rules.title: NJ Security Deposit cap (1.5 months' rent)
rules.requirement: A landlord may require a security deposit of no more than 1.5 times the monthly rent, plus the first month's rent at lease start (2.5 months total). Prepaid funds such as last month's rent count toward the deposit regardless of label.
rules.quoted_span: The landlord may only require one and one -half times the tenant’s monthly rent as security and the first month’s rent at the inception of the lease.
rules.key_value: 1.5 months' rent (2.5 months incl. first month's rent)
rules.effective_date_note: Effective date not stated in this document.
rules.conflict_note: Document part does not itself cite N.J.S.A. 46:8-21.2 for the cap; citation taken from known statute.

rules.title: NJ security deposit handling, interest and notice
rules.requirement: Deposits stay the tenant's property, held in trust in an interest-bearing New Jersey account. Interest belongs to the tenant, and the landlord must give written notice of the bank, amount, account type and rate within 30 days and annually.
rules.quoted_span: The security deposit money continues to be the property of the person making the deposit and must be held in trust by the person receiving the money.
rules.key_value: held in trust; interest to tenant; notice within 30 days

unverifiable_exemptions: seasonal use or rental (125 days or less)

rules.penalty: Tenant may apply deposit plus 7% interest to rent if notice or interest is not provided.

rules.title: NJ security deposit return within 30 days
rules.requirement: The landlord must return the deposit plus interest, less itemized deductions, within 30 days after the tenancy ends. A tenant may sue for double the amount wrongfully withheld.
rules.quoted_span: Within 30 days after the termination of a tenancy, a landlord must return the security deposit, plus interest earned less deductions, to the tenant
rules.key_value: 30 days; double damages if wrongfully withheld
rules.penalty: Double the amount wrongly withheld, plus court costs and reasonable attorney's fees; added civil penalty of $500-$2,000 for willful withholding from tenants receiving assistance.

rules.title: NJ Law Against Discrimination: source of lawful income
rules.requirement: Landlords may not discriminate in renting based on protected traits including source of lawful income. Exceptions include owner-occupied two-family dwellings and rooms in owner-occupied single homes.
rules.quoted_span: mental and physical disability, nationality, or source of lawful income.
rules.key_value: source of lawful income is a protected class
rules.penalty: Up to $10,000 for a first offense.

rules.title: NJ Newly Constructed Multiple Dwellings Law: 30-year exemption from local rent control
rules.requirement: Newly constructed multiple dwellings are exempt from local rent control ordinances for 30 years after construction is completed.
rules.quoted_span: newly constructed multiple dwellings shall be exempt from any local rent control ordinances for a period of 30 years following completion of construction of the building.

unverifiable_exemptions: government-subsidized rents may also be exempt

rules.conflict_note: State exemption limits the reach of local rent control ordinances.

rules.title: NJ Anti-Eviction Act: notice of rent increase and notice to quit
rules.requirement: A landlord must serve a valid notice to quit and notice of rent increase before evicting for nonpayment of an increased rent. The increase must not be unconscionable and must comply with local ordinances.
rules.quoted_span: before an owner can evict a tenant for nonpayment of an increased rent, they must first serve the tenant with a valid notice to quit and notice of rent increase.
rules.key_value: notice to quit and notice of rent increase required

unverifiable_exemptions: owner-occupied buildings with 2 or fewer units

no_rule_findings.finding: New Jersey has no statewide rent control or cap on rent increases. Municipalities may adopt rent control or leveling ordinances. Increases need proper notice and must not be unconscionable.
no_rule_findings.quoted_span: The State of New Jersey has no laws that establish, govern or control rents.

parsed.doc_summary: Part 2 of the NJ DCA Landlord-Tenant guide. It covers security deposits (cap, handling, return), LAD source-of-income discrimination, the absence of statewide rent control, the 30-year new-construction exemption from local rent control, and notice for rent increases.
